title: Liverpool’s Freddie Woodman ‘ready’ to start against Crystal Palace – Arne Slot
content:
Liverpool’s third-choice goalkeeper Freddie Woodman will start against Crystal Palace at Anfield on Saturday, Arne Slot has said.

With No 1 Alisson unlikely to be risked after a month out with a hamstring injury and deputy Giorgi Mamardashvili sidelined due to a wound in his leg, Woodman is set to start after making his Liverpool league debut as a substitute in Sunday’s victory over Everton.

“Giorgi will definitely not be available tomorrow and also not for the upcoming weeks,” Slot said. “Ali is close to a return so let’s see if tomorrow comes too early. That leaves, of course, Freddie Woodman as an option, who is definitely fit.

“We signed an experienced third goalkeeper for a reason. As well as being a good keeper, he’s a very good man and well liked in the dressing room, which is important in that role. He’s ready for it.”

Liverpool triggered their one-year option to keep Alisson at Anfield until the summer of 2027 but his future remains the subject of speculation after he was linked with a possible move for Juventus.

The Brazil international has been increasingly hampered by muscle problems in recent years. He missed 10 Premier League games last season and has already sat out eight this term.

“I am only focused on Ali’s short-term future and that is getting him back into goal as soon as possible,” Slot added. “We don’t react to rumours in this room. We only react when facts need to be told.”

Slot said feedback has been positive since striker Hugo Ekitike underwent surgery on a ruptured Achilles tendon last weekend. No timescale has yet been set for the France striker, who could be sidelined until 2027.

Joe Gomez is fit to return to the squad against Palace after missing the Merseyside derby.

More protests are planned over ticket price increases with supporters set to hold up yellow cards to owner Fenway Sports Group in the 13th minute of the game against Palace.

“Two weeks ago against Fulham there was also a protest but we felt the complete support of our fans throughout the whole game,” Slot said.

“A player like Freddie, if he has to start, definitely needs a lot of support from our fans.”
